newsitem.title: USA: Effingham County, Ga., to vote on two sales taxes.
newsitem.headline: Effingham County, Ga., to vote on two sales taxes.

text.p: Georgia's Effingham County School Board set a Sept 16 referendum on proposals to extend a one-cent special purpose sales tax and levy a new one-cent sales tax for schools, the Savannah Morning News said Monday.
Each one-cent tax would generate about $12.13 million over the five-year life of the tax.

Revenues from the special purpose tax are shared among the county and the cities of Springfield, Rincon and Guyton. The money is earmarked for road construction, police and fire equipment, drainage projects, water and sewer upgrades and recreation projects.

If the new tax for schools is approved, about $10 million would go for renovation and construction. The rest would be used to pay debt service on a lease-purchase agreement currently funded with property tax revenues.
Adopting the sales tax would allow the county to reduce its property tax rate by 2 mills, school officials said.
